upper_bound.quote: This is a common-refinement (overlay) construction: superimpose the concatenated intervals of $B$ on an initial segment of length $q$ of the concatenated intervals of $A$, cut both rows at the union of the division points and pair the corresponding cells; the bound on the number of cuts follows by counting the cells of the common refinement (standard; details omitted).
upper_bound.witness: The missing statement is a proof, for arbitrary disjoint nonempty collections A and B, that the proposed overlay is realizable using cuts within the original intervals and requires at most |A|+|B|-1 new cuts. The excerpt only sketches the overlay and explicitly omits the cut count, so bound (5) is not proved.
upper_bound.load_bearing: The upper-bound strategy stays within Xiang's allowance of n marks only by inserting bound (5) into count (13). Without a proved cut bound, the write-up has not established a legal reply for every Liu division.

parsed.notes: The stated formula is correct. The reduction and lower-bound graph argument are complete, but the all-n upper bound relies on an explicitly omitted proof of its crucial cutting lemma.
